{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Holiday Recipes|Holiday Recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

'''Holland tea cakes''' are simple flat [[Cookbook:Cookie|cookies]]. They are easy and quick to make. They are traditionally Christmas cookies but are good for any time. They last for a long time, so if you make too many they can be saved.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 stick [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], preferably melted
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], [[Cookbook:Separating Eggs|separated]]
*2 cups (280 g) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*1–2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (or to taste)
* Colored sugar or [[Cookbook:Nuts and Seeds|nuts]] for topping

==Procedure==
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (180°C). 
#Mix the butter and sugar until completely combined. Mix in the egg yolk, then the flour and cinnamon (preferably by hand, though this all can be done in a [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]] if you want).
#Pour batter into a cookie pan. Use the palm of your hand to spread and smooth it over the whole pan (this is the hardest part).
#[[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] on leftover egg white. Scatter your desired toppings evenly over the batter. 
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in preheated oven until cookies are golden brown (about 20 minutes). Remove, and let cool slightly. 
#Before they get too cool, cut them into small 1-inch (2.5 cm) squares.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Egg substitutes can be used in place of the egg yolk, but you still need egg white for the topping.
